title: Binary value bounded by a coin-run probability
statement: Let $p$ be an infinite Boolean sequence and let $K$ be a natural number. Define its binary value by $\sum_{i\ge0}(1_{p(i)=\mathrm{true}})2^{-(i+1)}$. Choose a Boolean word of length $K$ uniformly at random, and scan it against the first $K$ bits of $p$: at the first mismatch, return the corresponding bit of $p$; if there is no mismatch, return no value. The binary value of $p$ is at most the probability that this procedure returns true plus $2^{-K}$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a function from natural numbers to Boolean values
